- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.

- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 6 by 6 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 24 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates, and nothing on it is shown to you for free.
- write: write one line on the scroll, with your name on it. It uses your turn.
- read: read every line on the scroll you haven't read yet. It uses your turn.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: move, dig, write, read or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns A to F from west to east, rows 1 to 6 from south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time.

- move: walk one square north, east, south or west. A move off the island or onto a pirate fails without using your turn and you choose again; after 2 failed moves your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging a square may reveal the cave that holds the treasure.
- Only a pirate standing on that square knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

- You have exactly 4096 tokens to think. If you reach 4096 without making a tool call, your answer is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

notes.note:
I’m pirate-1. I searched A6, B6, C6, and D6; then I read the scroll and learned from pirate-2 that the cave was at C5. I headed there, was briefly blocked while other pirates stood on the open cave square, then entered on my turn 13 with 11 turns left, so my contribution was 100 + 11×10 = 210.

Things the designers should know:

- The scroll was essential; without pirate-2’s message I would have kept searching useless squares.
- Pirates standing on the open cave can block others from entering. I had to wait/read while pirate-3 and pirate-4 were on C5. That delays entry but is not a big problem; a useful convention is “enter immediately when you reach the cave so others can enter.”
- Reading periodically is worth it: I lost only one turn to reading, but it saved many turns of searching.
- A good team strategy is to divide the grid into clear search zones, and for whoever finds the cave to write its coordinates immediately, then enter as soon as possible.

Found the treasure at C5 on my 5th turn, wrote its location on the scroll for the other pirates, and then entered the cave on my 7th turn. My plan was to search row 5 systematically from A5 eastward; Pirate-1 appeared to be sweeping row 6, which suggested a simple row-based search pattern. I hope the other pirates read the scroll, make their way to C5, and enter quickly to maximize the crew’s score.

I’m Pirate-3, and I entered the cave at C5 on my turn 10, with 14 turns remaining.

What worked: Pirate-2 found the treasure, wrote its location on the scroll, and then presumably entered. When I read the scroll, I had a clear destination and could go straight to C5. That made coordination possible.

What cost us: I spent my first three turns reading an empty scroll. That was wasteful early on. A better rule might be: read only after a few turns have passed, or after someone signals they’ve found something. Still, the eventual message was enough to get me in quickly.

For the designers: the scroll communication mechanic is the heart of the game. The key strategic insight is that the pirate who finds the cave must *write the coordinates before entering*, and other pirates should *read periodically* to catch that message. Without writing, a discovery might help only the finder.

Also, the “turn remaining” bonus makes it important not to over-read early: reading empty scrolls is pure cost. A modest schedule — maybe read every 3–5 turns until a cave report appears — balances coordination with searching.

I’m Pirate-4. I entered the open cave at C5 on my turn 11, so I had 13 turns left: that contributes 100 + 10×13 = 230 points to the crew.

Key things from our run:
- Reading the scroll on my first turn was empty, but checking again later was decisive: Pirate-2 had written the cave location at C5, so I stopped searching and went straight there.
- Once the cave is found, the finder should write the coordinates immediately and then enter; it saved the rest of us from wasted digging.
- I briefly got blocked by Pirate-3 standing on C5. I stayed adjacent, used the forced waiting turn to dig C4, then moved onto the cave and entered as soon as the way cleared.
- Direct routing from B3 to C5 was: B3 → C3 → C4 → C5. I dug C4 while waiting for Pirate-3 to enter.
- Overall, the crew should prioritize: (1) search systematically, (2) announce cave finds loudly on the scroll, (3) converge immediately, and (4) avoid wasting turns trying to move through a pirate when a one-turn detour or a short wait is better.
